dumb_term_pill.tooltip: Otty is running with an untested TERM ("{term}"). A dumb terminal cannot execute escape sequences like "erase line", "clear screen", or cursor positioning. Change it in Settings → Shell → Terminal Identity, or install the matching terminfo entry.

data.apps_desc: What each tool carries between your machines. Turn one off to leave it on this device.
data.rescan_note: Tools installed on this device or run in Otty show up here on their own.
data.self_sync_body: {app} already carries these files between your machines. Two writers on one file fight, and the tool wins — it holds the file open and rewrites it from its own copy. Turn Otty's sync on only if you have switched {app}'s own off.
data.detail_empty: Nothing found for this app on this device yet.
data.item_refused: Holds a secret — this file is never uploaded
data.item_staged: Update waiting for your next pane
data.item_conflict: Changed here and elsewhere — pick one
data.secrets_desc: Names only. Values never leave your devices unencrypted; Otty's servers store ciphertext.
data.upsell_body: Your dotfiles and themes — synced, versioned and encrypted.
data.upsell_bullet_discover: Found the moment you install a tool
data.upsell_bullet_upload: Uploaded on its own, with history you can roll back
data.upsell_bullet_apply: Applied before your next shell opens, never under a running one
data.pass_create_body: Everything you sync is end-to-end encrypted with it. Your other devices ask for it once, when you turn sync on there.
data.pass_create_note: Otty never sees this password and cannot reset it. Forget it, and what is stored on the server cannot be opened — the devices already syncing keep working.
data.pass_unlock_body: The one chosen when sync was first turned on. This device needs it once to read what your other devices have synced.
data.pass_too_simple: Too easy to guess — avoid repeats, runs like 123456, and common passwords.
data.pass_mismatch: The two passwords do not match.
data.pass_wrong: That is not the sync password.
data.pass_exists: Another device set a sync password a moment ago. Enter that one.
data.pass_none: No sync password has been set yet. Choose one.
data.pass_failed: Could not reach Otty Anywhere. Try again.
data.kf_cloud_managed: sealed copy · not used to sync
data.kf_caption_managed: Files cross Otty Anywhere sealed, and sync never unseals them. Otty also keeps a sealed recovery copy of the key, handed only to a device you have just signed in on.
data.kf_caption_password: Files cross Otty Anywhere sealed. The key never leaves your devices, so Otty has nothing to open them with — a new device unseals the key with your password.
data.custody_body: Choose who keeps the key your dotfiles are encrypted with. You choose once, for the whole account.
data.custody_managed_body: Nothing to remember. Sign in on a new Mac and it syncs. Otty keeps a sealed recovery copy of the key, so losing every device loses nothing.
data.custody_password_body: Only your devices ever hold the key. Otty stores data it can't open. Forget the password and lose every device, and the synced copy is gone.
data.custody_none: Nobody has turned sync on for this account yet. Choose who keeps the key.
data.custody_missing: Your other devices can't open what {here} syncs yet — nobody has chosen who keeps the key.
data.custody_adopt_body: Sync is already on, and {here} encrypts with a key only it holds, so your phone and the web can't open what it syncs. Choose who keeps that key — once, for the whole account. Nothing is re-encrypted.
data.custody_saved: Saved. Your other devices can now open what syncs from here
data.reauth_body: This account's key is kept by Otty Anywhere, and it is only handed to a device that has just signed in. Sign in again on this device and the key follows.
data.key_rate_limited: Too many devices asked for the key recently. Try again in an hour.
data.transfer_desc: Works with or without a subscription — this is the way in, and the way out.
data.import_desc: Read a Ghostty, kitty or Alacritty config and bring over what Otty understands.
data.export_desc: Write Otty's settings out in another terminal's format.
data.privacy_desc: What Otty has remembered on this device, and how to throw it away.
data.net_desc: What Otty asks a server for on its own. Each one is switched where it lives.
data.net_updates_desc: Looks for a new version in the background
data.net_more_desc: Refreshes the list of our other apps, at most once a day
data.net_remote_desc: Connects to Otty Anywhere so your other devices can reach this one
data.net_sync_desc: Uploads and fetches your encrypted settings and dotfiles
data.group_desc: Find and manage the config your tools keep here. Backed up, versioned, carried between your machines.
data.empty_title: No dotfiles are managed on this device
data.empty_body: Otty can read your home directory and tell you which tools keep config here. You pick what travels — nothing leaves this device before you confirm.
data.gate_free_title: This device is not syncing yet
data.gate_free_body: You can scan and choose now — Otty Anywhere is what carries the result off this device.
data.gate_free_body_set: Your picks are saved on this device. Otty Anywhere is what backs them up, versions them, and puts them on your other machines.
data.gate_out_title: Sign in to pick this up
data.gate_out_body: Your picks live on this device. Signing in is what connects them to the copy your other machines already share.
data.wizard_scan_desc: Reading your home directory. Nothing is uploaded and nothing is changed.
data.wizard_failed: The scan could not finish. Nothing was changed.
data.wizard_review_title: {n} tools keep config on this device
data.wizard_review_desc: Uncheck anything you would rather keep to this machine.
data.wizard_note_ok: Secrets stay on this device; they are never uploaded.
data.wizard_note_blocked: Saved on this device on Confirm. Carrying them further needs Anywhere.
data.group_decide_note: {n} tools · left off until you say otherwise
data.group_secrets_note: never uploaded — they stay on this device
data.waiting_note: {n} tools · found since you set this up
data.tree_rule_only: Rule only — not on this device
data.tree_note_machine: Otty takes these lines out before upload and puts each machine's own back on the way down — no templates to write.
data.tree_note_secret: The rest of the file syncs. These values stay on this device.
data.tree_note_absent: Nothing to show until the file exists here; the rule is ready for it.
data.tree_note_no_match: Nothing in this file matches the rule, so it travels whole. The rule stands for the day something does.
data.status_local_sub: {n} tools · nothing has left this device
data.gate_sheet_off_body: Data Sync is off, so nothing leaves this device yet. Turn it on and {app} travels with the rest of your picks.
data.gate_sheet_out_body: Sync runs through your Otty Anywhere account. Sign in, then switch {app} on.
data.tools_load_failed: Couldn’t load your tools. Try again.
data.status_line_off: Off · everything stays on {here}. Your choices below are kept.
data.pending_over_limit: Held back — over the storage limit
data.toast_tool_backup: {app} is backed up — nothing on {here} gets overwritten
data.toast_when_on: takes effect once Sync & Backup is on
data.toast_restored: Restored — the copy it replaced is in history
data.self_sync_backup_note: Back up only is safe alongside it: Otty keeps versions and never writes to this machine.
data.alert_off_body: What you set here takes effect once it is on.
data.alert_new_body: It stays off until you turn it on.
data.alert_conflict_elsewhere: changed here and on another device.
data.alert_conflict_body: This file is paused until you pick one.
data.alert_refused_title: Nothing of this tool is uploaded.
data.alert_refused_body: Every file it keeps holds a secret, and Otty never uploads those.
data.alert_newer_body: Back up only never overwrites {here}, so it's waiting for you.
data.alert_self_body: Syncing them here too means two things write the same files.
data.tool_off_desc: Nothing is uploaded; the files stay where they are.
data.tool_backup_desc: Changes here go up with history. Nothing comes down.
data.tool_sync_desc: Changes go up, and changes from your other machines come down.
data.backup_only_desc: Never overwrite {here}. Bring a version over yourself when you want it.
data.restore_desc: Any saved version, from any of your machines.
data.add_file_home: Use a path inside your home folder, starting with ~/
data.rules_empty: None yet. Change a file's rule above and it lands here — it follows your account to every machine.
data.tree_note_backup: These lines are saved so you can rebuild this machine, and never applied to another one.
data.rule_whole_sub: Every machine gets the same copy
data.rule_backup_sub: Saved with history, never lands on another machine
data.rule_secret_sub: Never uploaded, even inside a synced folder
data.rule_saved_note: Saved to Your Rules. It follows your account.
data.rules_src_catalog: From the Otty dotfiles catalog, plus yours — where each file and line goes
data.rules_src_otty: Otty's own rules, built into the app — where each file and line goes
data.rules_src_inferred: Found in the usual places, plus yours — where each file and line goes
data.rules_docs: Built into Otty — read the docs
data.rules_platform: Goes to machines like this one
data.rules_platform_expl: Same OS and chip — these values depend on the kind of machine.
data.rules_backup_expl: Saved so you can rebuild {here}. Never applied to another machine.
data.rules_secret_expl: Otty refuses to upload these, even inside a synced folder.
data.versions_desc: Backups from all your machines, newest first
data.versions_note: Restoring replaces only the file you pick. The copy it replaces stays in history.

account.signed_out_desc: Signing in happens on the Remote tab, with the rest of Otty Anywhere.
account.devices_desc: Every device signed in to your Otty account. Remove one you no longer use or don't recognise: it is signed out and cut off from your other devices.
account.key_desc: Who keeps the key your synced data is encrypted with, and which devices have been handed it.
account.key_mode_managed_desc: Encrypted, and recoverable by signing in. Not end-to-end: Otty keeps a sealed copy of the key.
account.key_mode_password_desc: End-to-end encrypted. Only your devices hold the key.
account.key_release_fresh: received the key after signing in
account.key_releases_empty: No device has been handed the key yet.
account.remove_body: It is signed out of Otty Anywhere, can no longer reach your other devices, and stops syncing. Its files and settings stay on it.
account.remove_wipe_desc: Marks what this device backed up to your account for deletion, and has it clear its sync data the next time it is online. Marked backups can be recovered for 30 days by contacting us. Its files are never deleted.
account.sign_out_body: This device stops syncing and can no longer reach your other devices. Nothing on it is deleted, and signing back in picks up where it left off.
account.sign_out_body_mac: This Mac stops syncing and can no longer reach your other devices. Nothing on it is deleted, and signing back in picks up where it left off.
account.sign_out_wipe_desc: Marks the backups this device uploaded to your account for deletion; they can be recovered for 30 days by contacting us. Settings synced across your devices are kept.
account.sign_out_failed: Couldn't sign out. Check your connection and try again.
account.err_self: To take this device off your account, sign out instead.
account.err_not_trusted: This device can't remove others until it has been verified on your account.
account.err_step_up: Otty Anywhere wants to confirm it's you first. Try again from the dashboard (Manage).
account.err_unknown_device: That device is no longer on your account.
account.err_network: Couldn't reach Otty Anywhere. Check your connection and try again.

profiles.intro: A profile decides what a new pane launches and how it identifies itself. New panes use the default profile.
profiles.empty: No profiles yet. Add one to choose what new panes launch.
profiles.name: Name
profiles.shell_desc: The program the pane runs. This replaces the shell entirely — a WSL distro or an SSH target goes here.
profiles.command_desc: Typed into the shell once it has started and loaded its startup files. Use this for a program you want inside the shell, not instead of it.
profiles.cwd_desc: Where the pane starts. Leave empty to inherit. {{home}} expands to your home folder.
profiles.env_desc: One KEY=VALUE per line. Lines without an = are ignored.
profiles.elevate_desc: Launch the pane elevated. Windows will ask for consent each time.
profiles.shell_integration_desc: Load Otty's shell integration in panes this profile launches — prompt marks, working-directory tracking, command status and the `edit`/`view`/`jump` wrappers. Turning it off affects this profile only; the master switch stays in Settings → Shell.
profiles.theme_desc: Colour scheme for panes using this profile. Leave empty to follow the global setting.
profiles.theme_dark_desc: Used instead of Theme when the app follows the system's dark appearance.
profiles.title_prefix_desc: Prepended to the pane title. A title you set by hand always wins.
profiles.theme_follow_global_desc: Use the theme selected in Appearance settings
profiles.quick_access_desc: Pin this profile to the new-tab menu, the tray menu and the taskbar jump list.
profiles.default_row_desc: Make new panes launch this profile.
profiles.default_row_is_desc: New panes already launch this profile.
profiles.delete_desc: Removes it from the list and deletes its file.
profiles.delete_default_blocked: The default profile can't be deleted. Make another profile the default first.

recipe.replay_saved_desc: How recipes you saved in Otty replay their commands when opened.
recipe.replay_file_desc: How an external .ottyrecipe file replays its commands
recipe.replay_file_hint: Files come from elsewhere, so this defaults to being cautious.

general.os_integration_cli_description: Install the `otty` command into your PATH and customize shell integration.
general.full_disk_access_description: Needed to read or write protected files from Otty
general.full_disk_access_hint: DMGs, `~/Library`, Mail scripting. Otty itself works fine without it.
general.finder_integration_description: Add “Open in Otty” to Finder's right-click Services menu
general.finder_integration_hint: Rebind it under System Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts → Services.
general.set_default_terminal_for_apps: Set as Default Terminal for Common Apps
general.set_default_terminal_for_apps_descriptio: Make known editors and git GUIs open Otty, not Terminal.app
general.set_default_terminal_for_apps_hint: Rewrites each app's own “external terminal” setting.
general.external_apps_dialog_title: Set as Default Terminal for Common Apps
general.external_apps_dialog_body: Pick which apps should open Otty for their external terminal. Apps that aren't installed are skipped silently. Uninstall reverts each app to its built-in default.
general.external_app_vscode_insiders_desc: Same setting as VS Code, but for the Insiders channel.
general.external_app_sublime_text_desc: Writes `terminal` in the Terminal package's settings (requires the community Terminal package).
general.install_cli_description: Install the `otty` command into your PATH
general.install_cli_hint: Also installs shell completions and editor config highlighting.
general.omit_otty_prefix_description: Type `edit foo.txt` instead of `otty edit foo.txt`
general.omit_otty_prefix_hint: In shells launched by Otty. Adds shell functions for `edit`, `view`, `watch`, `jump` and `learn`.
general.cli_allow_overwrite_hint: Applies when Omit Prefix or Custom Aliases is on. Off keeps whatever you already defined.
general.cli_custom_aliases_hint: Applies to shells launched by Otty, at shell init — open a new shell after editing.
general.cli_alias_dialog_empty: No aliases yet. Click "+ Add alias" to create one.
general.cli_learn_more_description: Read the full Otty CLI usage guide online.
general.auto_update_description: Check for updates in the background and prompt to install
general.auto_update_hint: Also refreshes the recommended apps list. Turn it off to stay fully offline.
general.auto_update_blocked_env: Automatic checks are off: OTTY_NO_UPDATE_CHECK is set.
general.auto_update_blocked_package: Automatic checks are off: your package manager updates this copy of Otty.
general.update_status_up_to_date: Up to date — $1 is the latest.
general.update_status_ready_to_install: Ready to install. Quit and install to apply.
general.stay_in_tray_desc: Closing the last window hides it in the tray instead of quitting, so its tabs keep running. Click the tray icon to bring it back. Off quits with the last window.
general.show_tray_icon_desc: Put otty in the notification area. Its menu shows tabs waiting on you, the open windows, and Quick Access.
general.show_tray_icon_forced_desc: Always on while "Stay in Tray" is set — otherwise a window-less otty would have no way back.
general.tray_quick_access_desc: The pinned folders, recipes, SSH hosts and profiles the tray menu, the taskbar jump list and the new-tab menu offer. Edited under View.
general.new_window_when_all_windows_closed: New Window When All Windows Closed
general.new_window_when_all_windows_closed_disab: Unavailable while "Quit When All Windows Closed" is on.
general.new_window_when_all_windows_closed_needs: Needs "Stay in Tray" — otty quits with its last window otherwise.
general.window_hide_dirty_indicator_description: Never show the unsaved/running dot on the window close button.

editor.line_wrap_desc: Wrap long lines instead of scrolling horizontally
editor.show_line_numbers_desc: Display the line-number gutter in text panes
editor.visible_whitespace_desc: Render spaces, tabs, and newlines as visible glyphs
editor.tab_size_desc: Visual width of a tab character, in columns
editor.scroll_past_end_desc: Allow scrolling past the last line in the editor
editor.scroll_past_end_hint: The terminal's own scroll-past-end is under Controls.
editor.vim_desc: Modal editing in file and editor panes
editor.vim_hint: Panes open in Normal mode: h j k l to move, i / a to insert, v for Visual, d / c / y operators. Esc returns to Normal.
editor.open_with_desc: Whether Cmd+click hands files to an Otty pane or an external app
editor.open_with_hint: Applies to the right-click Open items too. The app list itself is under Controls.
editor.open_with_desc_win: Whether Ctrl+click and the right-click Open items hand a URL or file path to an Otty pane or to an external app — set under Controls
editor.default_to_preview_readonly_desc: Markdown / SVG / HTML open as a rendered preview
editor.default_to_preview_readonly_hint: File panes also start read-only. Turn this off to open the source instead, ready to edit.

remote.subtitle: Who can reach this device, which machines you work on, and what Otty may do on the other end.

anywhere.title: Otty Anywhere
anywhere.pitch: Free for one device and one host. Pro adds unlimited devices, handing a session to your phone, and encrypted setup sync.
anywhere.handoff_title: Pick it up on your phone
anywhere.handoff_body: An agent keeps running here. Your phone buzzes when it finishes or needs an answer, and you reply from the lock screen.
anywhere.handoff_alt: A session on the Mac hands off to a phone, which shows a notification and an approval prompt
anywhere.sync_body: Themes, key bindings, recipes and shell dotfiles follow you onto every Mac, every phone and every host you log into.
anywhere.sync_alt: Config flowing between a laptop, a phone and a server through a shared store

takeover.caption_off: Nothing here can be taken over. This device can still take over your others, and approve new ones.
takeover.caption_ask: Each time a device wants a pane, Allow or Deny appears here. No answer in 60 seconds counts as Deny.
takeover.caption_always: Your devices can take over any pane without asking.
takeover.timeout_desc: An idle shared session ends after this long. A share link with a PIN stays valid as long.
takeover.security_desc: Which new devices may join your account. Set on the Account tab.
takeover.security_signed_out_desc: Sign in to use your account's devices

devices.notifications_desc: When an agent here finishes or needs an answer, this device gets a notification.
devices.unpair_confirm: This device will have to scan a new code.
devices.empty: No other devices signed in yet.
devices.hint: Sign in to the same Otty account on each device. You can also add a device with a sign-in code from this device.
devices.needs_pro_title: The free plan connects your first two devices. Pro reaches this one too.
devices.pro_hint: On the free plan your first two devices reach each other; the rest stay listed, greyed out. Pro reaches all of them.
devices.account_note: This device is on your Otty account. Deleting it signs it out and disconnects it from your other devices.

hosts.visibility_shown_title: Offered in ssh completion, Open Quickly and the Host menu · click to hide
hosts.visibility_hidden_title: Hidden from those lists — the host still works · click to show
hosts.filter_empty: No hosts from that source yet.
hosts.hint: Hosts come from ~/.ssh/config and ~/.config/otty/ssh_config. Otty adds icons, colours and forwarding rules on top and never rewrites lines you typed yourself. Hover any icon for its name. A dash under Helper means you turned it down — a choice, not a fault; red is kept for things that are actually broken.
hosts.add_hostname_hint: Paste a whole `ssh …` command here and the fields fill themselves in.
hosts.add_alias_hint: What you type after `ssh`. Suggested from the address.
hosts.add_from_command: Read from the command you pasted.
hosts.add_from_command_key: It signs in with {path}, which is saved with the host.
hosts.add_from_command_ignored: Not saved, this form has no place for it: {options}
hosts.add_key_failed: The host was added, but its key could not be saved: {error}
hosts.add_note: Otty writes this to its own file and never edits ~/.ssh/config. How it signs in comes next — and the Key column asks again whenever you want to change it.
hosts.add_alias_taken: A host with that name already exists.
hosts.add_alias_invalid: A name cannot contain spaces, quotes or #, or start with a dash.
hosts.add_hostname_invalid: An address cannot contain spaces, quotes or #.
hosts.add_port_invalid: A port is a number from 1 to 65535.
hosts.key_password_saved: Password — saved in the keychain · click to change
hosts.key_password_missing: Set to sign in with a password, but none is saved · click to fix
hosts.key_unknown_change: No key recorded · click to choose one
hosts.cred_key_hint: One private key, and only that one — ssh stops offering the others.
hosts.cred_agent_hint: Whatever keys your running agent holds. This is what ssh does by default.
hosts.cred_1password_hint: 1Password's SSH agent answers instead of a key on disk.
hosts.cred_password_hint: Saved in your keychain and typed for you when ssh asks.
hosts.cred_password_note: The password goes to your keychain, never into a config file. Otty fills it in through ssh’s own askpass helper when you connect from a pane.
hosts.cred_inherit: Leave it to the config file
hosts.cred_inherit_hint: Removes what Otty wrote and lets your ssh config decide again.
hosts.cred_writes_otty: Written to ~/.config/otty/ssh_config, the file this host already lives in.
hosts.cred_writes_override: Written to ~/.config/otty/ssh_config as an override. Your ~/.ssh/config is not touched — Otty’s file is Included above it, so ssh reads this first.
hosts.helper_unsupported: This build ships no helper for that platform
hosts.helper_caps: The helper adds completions, host stats, the file tree and code search. Otty writes one binary to ~/.local/share/otty and touches nothing else.
hosts.check_failed: The check could not be run.
hosts.wiz_just_added: “{alias}” is saved. It still needs a way to sign in — pick one now, or leave it and use the Key column whenever you are ready.
hosts.wiz_keysource_existing: Use a key I already have
hosts.wiz_keysource_new_hint: Ed25519 by default. Otty runs ssh-keygen and offers to send the public half over.
hosts.wiz_keypick_empty: No private keys in ~/.ssh yet. Go back and generate one.
hosts.wiz_keypick_hint: “On host” means this key’s public half is in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys there — checked over the connection Otty already has open, never by opening a new one.
hosts.wiz_onhost_unknown: Otty has no live session on this host, so it cannot say which of these the host already knows — and it will not open a connection to find out.
hosts.wiz_new_type_hint: Ed25519 unless the host is old enough to refuse it.
hosts.wiz_new_file_hint: A name, not a path — it is written into ~/.ssh, mode 600.
hosts.wiz_new_remember: Remember the passphrase in my keychain
hosts.wiz_new_remember_hint: The key itself stays in ~/.ssh — only the passphrase goes to your login keychain. Otty writes AddKeysToAgent and UseKeychain for this host, so ssh unlocks the key for you after a restart instead of asking again.
hosts.wiz_agent_add_failed: The key was written, but ssh-add would not take it: {message}
hosts.wiz_agent_existing: Use a key the agent already holds
hosts.wiz_agent_new_hint: New key, then ssh-add — so it is there next time without asking.
hosts.wiz_agent_pins_hint: Picking one writes IdentitiesOnly, so ssh offers that key first instead of every key the agent holds — which is what burns MaxAuthTries on a host that only knows one of them.
hosts.wiz_agentpick_hint: Straight from ssh-add -l. Otty writes IdentityAgent SSH_AUTH_SOCK for this host, so ssh offers the agent’s keys — this one among them.
hosts.wiz_agent_empty: Your agent holds no keys yet. Go back and generate one; Otty will ssh-add it for you.
hosts.wiz_op_hint: The same ssh-add -l as the agent step, pointed at 1Password’s socket instead of $SSH_AUTH_SOCK.
hosts.wiz_op_off_note: Nothing is listening on the agent socket, so there are no keys to choose from yet.
hosts.wiz_op_off_hint: Turn it on in 1Password → Developer → Use the SSH agent. Otty looks for it at:
hosts.wiz_op_empty: 1Password’s agent is running but holds no SSH keys.
hosts.wiz_password_note: The config will say PubkeyAuthentication no for this host, so ssh stops offering keys before asking.
hosts.wiz_inherit_title: Leave it to the config file
hosts.wiz_inherit_hint: These are the lines Otty wrote for {host}. Removing them puts the host back under whatever your own config says.
hosts.wiz_inherit_nothing: Otty has written nothing for this host, so there is nothing to remove.
hosts.wiz_inherit_note: Your ~/.ssh/config is not touched — it never was.
hosts.wiz_copy_title: The host doesn’t know this key yet
hosts.wiz_copy_hint: A key only works once its public half is in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on {host}. Otty can put it there in a new tab — you may be asked for the host’s password once.
hosts.wiz_copy_note: Skip and the key is still saved — the row will just show it as not on host until you do this.
hosts.wiz_done_agent: {host} now signs in with a key from your agent.
hosts.wiz_done_password: {host} now signs in with a password from your keychain.
hosts.wiz_done_inherit: {host} is back under whatever your own config says.
hosts.wiz_keychain_saved: The passphrase is in your login keychain; the key itself is still the file in ~/.ssh.

ssh.helper_policy: Install the Otty helper on remote hosts
ssh.helper_policy_desc: Needed for completions, host stats, the file tree and code search
ssh.helper_hint_windows: On Windows this installs only the remote `otty` command — a small script at ~/.local/share/otty/bin/otty — so `otty view` and `otty jump` typed on the host reach this Otty. It needs a host that takes your key or ssh-agent; a password-only host is never asked.
ssh.helper_hint: Without the helper, a remote pane still has prompt marks, working-directory tracking, file open & save, git status and port forwarding. Completions fall back to your shell's own; host stats and the remote file tree stay unavailable. Otty writes one binary to ~/.local/share/otty and touches nothing else.

pair.desktop_title: Pick it up on your other computer
pair.desktop_body: An agent keeps running here. Continue the session from your other computer and respond when it needs your input.
pair.desktop_alt: A terminal session handed off from one computer to another, with a confirmation on the receiving screen
pair.title: Add a device
pair.description: Scan this code on your other device to sign it in to your Otty account. Only share it with a device you own.
pair.waiting: Waiting for a device to scan…
pair.failed: Could not finish device sign-in. Try again.
pair.payload_label: Or paste this on the other device
pair.paste_hint: On a Mac or PC, choose Sign in with a device code and paste this link.
pair.account_required: Sign in and verify this device before adding another device. If you are using a code, get it from an already signed-in device.
pair.account_mismatch: This device is signed in to a different account. Sign out first, then use the device code.
pair.invalid_code: This sign-in code is invalid, expired, or already used. Get a new code from your other device.
pair.not_confirmed: Device sign-in has not completed. Check your other device and try again.
pair.signin_description: On an already signed-in device, open My Devices → Add a device. Paste its sign-in link here to join the same account.

advanced.title: Advanced
advanced.desc: Self-hosting and firewall settings. Leave these alone unless you run your own relay.
advanced.relay_url_desc: Signalling server used for pairing and for reaching devices that cannot connect directly
advanced.direct_port_desc: Port the direct listener binds so your devices can skip the relay. 0 picks a free port.

security.verify_desc: A device that signs in to your account reaches nothing until one of your devices approves it.
security.verify_desc_totp: A device that signs in reaches nothing until one of your devices approves it, or you enter an authenticator code.
security.verify_off_desc: Off — anyone who signs in to your account reaches your devices straight away.
security.pending_title: This device is waiting to be verified
security.pending_desc: It can't reach your other devices yet. Approve it on one of them, or enter a code.
security.pending_wait: Joins your account {when}, unless someone denies it.
security.request_web_desc: Wants to change your account's devices or security
security.request_recovering: Recovering access — joins {when} unless you deny it
security.request_only_if: Only allow this if you are signing in there right now.
security.request_only_if_web: Only allow this if you are doing that in a browser right now.
security.request_failed_codes: Someone entered {n} wrong codes for this sign-in.
security.sheet_desc: How a new device proves it's yours
security.method_device_desc: Each of your trusted devices shows Allow / Deny when a new one signs in.
security.method_totp_desc: A six-digit code from 1Password, Google Authenticator or any TOTP app.
security.recovery_desc: One-time codes for when you have neither a trusted device nor the app.
security.setup_scan: Scan the code with your authenticator app, or type the setup key into it.
security.setup_code: Then enter the six-digit code the app shows.
security.codes_body: Each code works once, for when you have neither a trusted device nor the app. Keep them in your password manager — this is the only time they are shown.
security.prove_body: Enter a code from your authenticator app, or one of your recovery codes.
security.prove_remove_body: Enter a code from your authenticator app, or a recovery code. Your recovery codes stop working along with it.
security.prove_regen_body: Enter a code from your authenticator app. The recovery codes you have now stop working.
security.reauth_title: Sign in again to turn this off
security.reauth_body: Turning verification off needs a sign-in from the last 15 minutes. Otty opens your browser — come back here when it's done.
security.bad_code: That code didn't work. Check it and try again.
security.rate_limited: Too many tries. Wait a few minutes, then try again.
security.verification_locked: This device tried too many codes and is locked. Approve it from one of your other devices.
security.too_many_requests: Too many devices are waiting to join this account. Answer or deny them first.
security.recovery_unavailable: This account uses an authenticator app, so the waiting period isn't available. Use a recovery code instead.
security.not_linked: This sign-in has expired. Sign in again to verify this device.
security.failed: That didn't go through. Check your connection and try again.
security.verify_waiting: Waiting for one of your devices to approve…
security.verify_waiting_desc: Your trusted devices are each asking whether to let “{name}” in.
security.verify_code_desc: A code from your authenticator app, or one of your recovery codes.
security.cant_use: I can't use any of these
security.recover_body: Otty emails {email} right away and again every day, with a link to cancel. If nobody cancels it there or denies it on one of your devices, this device joins your account in 72 hours.
security.recover_note: Nothing else to do — leave this device signed in.
security.recover_started: This device joins your account {when}, unless someone cancels it from the email or denies it on one of your devices.
security.verified: Verified. This device is part of your account now.

intro.title: How should new devices join your account?
intro.body: Devices on the same Otty account reach each other with no pairing and no PIN. That makes a sign-in the key — so choose whether a new one has to be confirmed.
intro.verify_body: A new sign-in waits until you approve it on one of your devices, or enter a code from an authenticator app.
intro.tag_verify: Approve on a device or authenticator
intro.off_body: A new sign-in reaches your devices straight away.
intro.also_totp: Also set up an authenticator app
intro.signed_out_title: Choose how devices find this one
intro.signed_out_body: Sign in to reach your other devices, or use a sign-in code from a device already on your account.
intro.signin_body: Your devices on the same account reach each other. New ones are verified first.
intro.tag_every_device: Every device you sign in on
intro.pair_title: Sign in with a device code
intro.pair_body: Use a code from an already signed-in device to join the same Otty account.
intro.dia_caption_verify: A new sign-in knocks. One of your devices — or a code from your authenticator — lets it in.
intro.dia_caption_off: A new sign-in walks straight in: whoever can sign in to your account reaches your devices.
intro.dia_caption_signin: Sign in on each of your devices and they find each other. A new one is verified first.
intro.dia_caption_pair: A code from your signed-in device signs this device in to the same account.

controls.option_as_alt_desc: Treat Option as Alt/Meta so apps see Esc-prefixed sequences
controls.option_as_alt_hint: Off keeps Option for typing accented characters (é, ©…).
controls.ctrl_shortcuts_desc: A bare Ctrl chord is both a Windows shortcut and the control byte the shell reads. Pick how to tell them apart. In every mode but “always send to shell”, the Windows editing chords count as shortcuts — Ctrl+C copy, Ctrl+V paste, Ctrl+F find, Ctrl+T new tab, Ctrl+W close — as does any bare Ctrl chord you bind yourself under Key Bindings. Everything else (Ctrl+A, Ctrl+R, Ctrl+D…) always reaches the shell instantly, whatever this is set to.
controls.ctrl_c_action_desc: Whether Ctrl+C counts as a Windows shortcut. Copying on a selection is what Windows Terminal and VS Code do; with nothing selected it goes straight to the shell as ^C. The selection decides on its own — Ctrl+C is never put behind a hold or a Ctrl side, because that is the key you reach for to stop a runaway process.
controls.ctrl_c_shortcut_link_desc: Whether Ctrl+C copies the selection or sends ^C to the shell — set under Keyboard
controls.focus_follows_mouse_desc: Focus the pane under the mouse cursor automatically
controls.right_click_action_desc: What right-click does in the terminal viewport
controls.right_click_action_hint: Ctrl+right-click always opens the menu, whatever this is set to.
controls.mouse_hide_while_typing_desc: Hide the mouse cursor while the keyboard is in use
controls.mouse_shift_to_select_desc: Hold Shift to select text even when the running app captures the mouse
controls.bypass_mouse_reporting_desc: Hold to select text or open a link past a mouse-capturing app
controls.bypass_mouse_reporting_hint: Full-screen apps like vim or tmux capture the mouse; this modifier lets the click reach Otty instead.
controls.link_click_over_mouse_mode: Ctrl-Click Opens Links in Mouse Mode
controls.link_click_over_mouse_mode_desc: Ctrl-click opens a link even while an app captures the mouse
controls.link_click_over_mouse_mode_hint: Matches Windows Terminal. When off, the click is sent to the app instead.
controls.cursor_click_to_move_desc: Click in the prompt to move the shell cursor — sends arrow keys across soft-wrapped rows
controls.link_open_with_desc: Where Cmd+click and the right-click "Open Link" item open a URL
controls.link_open_with_desc_win: Where Ctrl+click and the right-click "Open Link" item open a URL
controls.file_open_with_desc: Where Cmd+click and the right-click "Open File" item open a file path
controls.file_open_with_desc_win: Where Ctrl+click and the right-click "Open File" item open a file path
controls.folder_open_with_desc: Where Cmd+click and the right-click "Open Folder" item open a folder path
controls.folder_open_with_desc_win: Where Ctrl+click and the right-click "Open Folder" item open a folder path
controls.default_git_client_desc: The git GUI opened from the Details ▸ Git toolbar
controls.open_with_apps_desc: The apps offered in every “Open in…” menu
controls.open_with_apps_hint: Also used by the Details panel and the command palette. Pre-filled with the editors installed on this machine — remove the ones you don't want, add your own.
controls.open_with_presets_hint: Put the defaults back — every editor Otty knows about that is installed on this machine.
controls.open_with_dialog_empty: Nothing here yet, so no "Open in…" entry shows anywhere. Add an app, a TUI command such as yazi, or click "Add Presets" to bring the defaults back.
controls.link_schemes_desc: Which URL schemes become clickable on Cmd-hover
controls.link_schemes_hint: http(s), file and mailto are always detected; “Custom” adds your own.
controls.link_schemes_desc_win: Which URL schemes get underlined on hover and opened with Ctrl+click. http(s), file and mailto are always detected; "Custom" adds your own.
controls.link_schemes_custom_list_desc: URL schemes to additionally detect (e.g. codex, ssh, vscode)
controls.link_schemes_dialog_desc: Extra URL schemes to auto-detect and make clickable. Enter bare scheme names like "codex" or "ssh" — no "://" needed.
controls.link_schemes_empty: No custom schemes yet — add one below.
controls.link_previews_desc: Show the full path or URL while Cmd-hovering a link
controls.link_previews_hint: A pill in the bottom corner. Turning it off keeps links clickable — it only hides the preview.
controls.link_previews_desc_win: While hovering a link, show a pill in the bottom corner with its full path or URL and a reminder that Ctrl+Click opens it. Disabling it keeps links clickable but hides the preview.
controls.reset_security_warnings_hint: The confirmation dialog comes back for external links, custom schemes and executables.
controls.auto_secure_input_desc: Turn on Secure Keyboard Entry at a password prompt
controls.auto_secure_input_hint: A prompt is detected as canonical mode without echo. macOS Secure Keyboard Entry stops other apps from reading your keystrokes.
controls.secure_input_indication_desc: Show a pill in the title bar while Secure Keyboard Entry is active
controls.scroll_past_end_desc: Where the last row settles when you scroll past the bottom
controls.scroll_past_end_hint: Anchors the last row or the cursor at the viewport top or middle. Always off on the alternate screen.
controls.scroll_past_first_line_desc: Where the first row settles when you scroll above the top
controls.scroll_past_first_line_hint: Anchors it at the viewport bottom or middle. “Same as Scroll Past Last Line” mirrors that setting.
controls.scroll_past_first_line_same: Same as Scroll Past Last Line
controls.scroll_smooth_desc: Scroll by pixel instead of snapping row by row
controls.scroll_smooth_hint: The offset realigns to a row boundary when the gesture ends.
controls.copy_on_select_desc: Copy text to the clipboard automatically when you finish selecting
controls.trim_trailing_spaces_desc: Strip trailing whitespace from each line when copying
controls.paste_protection_desc: Warn when pasted text would auto-execute commands
controls.paste_protection_hint: Triggered by interior newlines or control characters.
controls.paste_bracketed_safe_desc: Skip the paste warning when the running app supports bracketed paste mode
controls.selection_clear_on_typing_desc: Clear the active selection when you type
controls.selection_clear_on_copy_desc: Clear the active selection after Cmd+C, the copy menu, or right-click copy
controls.selection_clear_on_copy_desc_win: Clear the active selection after Ctrl+C, the copy menu, or right-click copy
controls.selection_clear_on_copy_disabled_desc: Disabled while Copy on Select is on — the selection is preserved after copy
controls.selection_backspace_deletes_desc: Backspace deletes the selection, not one character
controls.selection_backspace_deletes_hint: Applies when text is selected on the prompt line.
controls.history_scope_desc: Whether panes share command history as you type
controls.history_scope_hint: Applied by shell integration at runtime — it overrides your shell's own history options, and only inside Otty.
controls.history_up_arrow_desc: What Up recalls at the prompt
controls.history_up_arrow_hint: Applied by shell integration at runtime — it rebinds the arrow keys, and only inside Otty.
controls.history_arrow_link_desc: What the arrow keys bring back at the prompt — set under Command History

shell.windows_sudo_desc: Windows ships a `sudo` command for running one command as Administrator, off until you enable it under For developers. Pick the inline mode there and it runs in the current pane; the other modes open a separate window. (Otty's own Run as Administrator needs none of this.)
shell.shift_arrow_select_desc: Select text with Shift+Arrow keys instead of sending escape sequences
shell.ssh_integration_desc: Forward environment and terminfo over SSH
shell.ssh_integration_hint: Wraps SSH commands, and enables remote file and git access via ControlMaster.
shell.ssh_integration_disable_body: Otty will stop wrapping your `ssh` command. Environment forwarding, remote terminfo install, and ControlMaster-based remote file/git access will no longer be set up. You can turn it back on anytime.
shell.shell_integration_desc: Powers prompt marks, CWD tracking and command status
shell.shell_integration_hint: Also installs the `edit` / `view` / `jump` wrappers. Adds one line to your shell startup files.
shell.shell_integration_profile_inert: Otty has no integration for this shell
shell.requires_integration_warning: Shell Integration is off — this feature relies on it and won’t work until you turn it back on in the Shell tab.
shell.shell_integration_disable_body: Otty will remove its line from your shell startup files. Prompt marks, command status, working-directory tracking, the `edit`/`view`/`jump` wrappers, custom aliases and SSH integration will stop working in Otty shells. You can turn it back on anytime.
shell.shell_integration_disable_shell_body: Otty will stop integrating your `{shell}` sessions — prompt marks, command status, working-directory tracking and the `edit`/`view`/`jump` wrappers stop working there, and any managed block Otty added to `{shell}`'s startup files is removed. Your other shells and SSH integration are unaffected. You can turn it back on anytime.
shell.frecency_auto_record_desc: Record every folder you visit into the jump database
shell.frecency_auto_record_hint: Every CWD change in an Otty pane. Powers `otty jump` and the Folders tab in Open Quickly.
shell.tracked_ignored_folders_desc: Folders the jump database knows about
shell.tracked_ignored_folders_hint: Open the manager to browse them, or to move folders between the tracked and ignored lists.
shell.zoxide_enabled_desc: Also forget paths from your local `zoxide` database
shell.zoxide_enabled_hint: Applies when you run `otty ignore` or “Forget this folder”, if zoxide is installed.
shell.restore_multiplayer_desc: Reattach multiplexer sessions when restoring a window. Currently only tmux is supported.
shell.restore_code_agents_desc: Resume Claude / Codex / OpenCode sessions when restoring a terminal
shell.terminal_resume_protocol_desc: Let programs declare how Otty should relaunch them
shell.terminal_resume_protocol_hint: Editors, SSH and coding agents, via OSC 88 — so Otty can restore them on restart.
shell.restore_processes_desc: Re-launch the command that was running in each pane when a window is restored
shell.command_whitelist_desc: Commands eligible for re-run, matched as whitespace-delimited prefixes
shell.command_whitelist_dialog_desc: Commands eligible for re-run on restore. Matched as whitespace-delimited prefixes, so "npm run dev" matches "npm run dev --port 3000".
shell.command_whitelist_empty: No commands yet — add one below.
shell.sound_shell_desc: Allow shell apps to play sounds via BEL character
shell.sound_on_error_desc: Beep when a command exits with non-zero status
shell.notification_permission_desc_win: Windows manages notifications per app in Settings — turn Otty's off there if you don't want banners.
shell.notification_perm_banner_none: Allowed, but banner style is set to None — banners won’t appear
shell.notification_perm_allowed: Otty is allowed to send notifications
shell.notification_perm_denied: Turned off in System Settings — banners won’t appear
shell.notification_shell_desc: Allow shell apps to send system notifications
shell.notify_on_finish_desc: Notify when a background command finishes
shell.notify_on_watch_finish_desc: Notify when an `otty watch`-wrapped command finishes
shell.notify_foreground_desc: Banner behavior while otty is the foreground app
shell.notify_foreground_tab_unfocused: Only when source tab is unfocused
shell.notification_attention_desc: Bounce the Dock icon when a notification arrives and Otty isn't focused
shell.notify_sound_desc: Play a sound for the selected notification categories. Silent by default.
shell.term_desc: What kind of terminal to advertise to child processes
shell.term_hint: Auto is the safe default; richer values unlock features in apps that key off $TERM.
shell.term_custom_hint: If your system's terminfo database has this entry, it will be used as-is. Otherwise Otty falls back to xterm-256color so line editing (backspace, autocomplete redraw) keeps working.
shell.manage_folders_empty_tracked: No tracked folders yet. Visit a directory in any Otty pane to start building the jump database.
shell.manage_folders_empty_ignored: No ignored folders. Use the Ignore button to keep paths out of jump results.
shell.manage_folders_clear_confirm_body: This removes every folder from the jump database. Visits will be re-learned as you `cd` around.
shell.manage_folders_clear_confirm_ignored_bod: This forgets every ignored path. They'll be eligible for jump results again the next time you visit them.
shell.autocomplete_shortcut_desc: Accepts a single match or the selected candidate
shell.autocomplete_shortcut_hint: The key that takes the suggestion when exactly one match is showing, or when you have picked a candidate out of the panel. With Right Arrow, Tab always goes to your shell's own completion.
shell.show_candidates_desc: When to show the candidate panel
shell.inline_suggestion_desc: A faded preview when one suggestion clearly leads
shell.inline_suggestion_desc_win: A faded preview after the cursor: Otty's when one suggestion clearly leads, or PSReadLine's history prediction first
shell.on_device_learning_desc: Learns from what you run. Nothing leaves this device.
shell.on_device_learning_hint: Learns which arguments you use most and the whole command lines themselves, plus tools' --help output and project README files. All of it stays on this device — nothing is uploaded.
shell.skip_secrets_desc: Never record a command that looks like a credential
shell.skip_secrets_hint: A command that looks like it carries a password, token or API key. Applies to new commands only; to keep one deliberately, run `otty learn '<cmd>'`.
shell.desc_lang_desc: Language for spec descriptions in the candidate panel and inline preview
shell.clear_autocomplete_desc: Wipe what autocomplete has learned about you. Built-in CLI specs are kept.
shell.clear_autocomplete_dialog_body: Select what to remove. This can't be undone.
shell.clear_autocomplete_opt_history_desc: Per-argument frequency you've built up while typing.
shell.clear_autocomplete_opt_helpprobe_desc: Options and subcommands learned automatically from tools you've used.
shell.clear_autocomplete_opt_learnedfolder_des: Commands you saved with `otty learn` in each folder.
shell.clear_autocomplete_opt_learnedspecs_desc: Locally-promoted command specs that override the bundled defaults.

appearance.auto_theme_dark_mode: Use separated theme for dark mode
appearance.auto_theme_dark_mode_hint: The theme above is used in light mode, the dark theme below in dark mode.
appearance.theme_inactive_hint_light: Will be applied when the system switches to light mode.
appearance.theme_inactive_hint_dark: Will be applied when the system switches to dark mode.
appearance.theme_queued_toast_light: Theme saved — it will take effect when the system switches to light mode.
appearance.theme_queued_toast_dark: Theme saved — it will take effect when the system switches to dark mode.
appearance.font_family_theme_desc: Saved into the active theme's TOML
appearance.font_family_theme_light_desc: Saved into the light theme's TOML
appearance.font_family_theme_dark_desc: Saved into the dark theme's TOML
appearance.font_family_fallback_desc: Comma-separated; used when a glyph is missing
appearance.text_rendering_desc: How DirectWrite rasterizes the grid. ClearType is subpixel-tuned for LCDs; Natural is smoother at large sizes.
appearance.line_height_desc: Scale row height by this multiplier (1.0 = font default)
appearance.adjust_cell_height_desc: Add this many pixels to each row (negative shrinks)
appearance.import_theme_hint: Imports a .itermcolors file, or a Kitty / Alacritty / Ghostty color file, as a new theme.
appearance.cursor_preview_note: Live preview of your cursor color, style, opacity and blink behavior.
appearance.cursor_blink_desc: Whether the cursor blinks, and whether programs may change it
appearance.cursor_blink_default_note: The `Default` options set the initial blink state but let a program override it (DECSCUSR `\e[5 q`/`\e[2 q`, DEC mode 12). The `Always` options pin the cursor and ignore program control.
appearance.cursor_animation_note: Smooth glides the caret on same-row moves and adds an overshoot on click/focus.
appearance.show_tab_bar_desc: When to show the tab bar in Tabs Top / Tabs Bottom layouts
appearance.show_tabs_panel_desc: When to show the tabs panel in Sidebar layout
appearance.window_size_desc: How new windows decide their initial dimensions.
appearance.unfocused_split_opacity_desc: How much split panes fade when they don’t have focus
appearance.unfocused_split_opacity_hint: Set to 1.00 to keep every pane fully visible.
appearance.icon_animate_progress_desc: Spin the right eye while a session is working
appearance.icon_animate_progress_warning: Increases CPU and battery use while sessions are running
appearance.icon_animate_progress_dialog_body:
While a session is working, the Dock icon repaints on a timer. Each repaint re-rasters the icon on the CPU and pushes it to the system, which keeps your laptop awake and noticeably increases battery use.

Only enable this if you find the spinning eye useful enough to justify the cost.
appearance.icon_error_badge_desc: Tint the icon red on failure; click Dock to jump to the failing tab
appearance.icon_bounce_desc: Bounce the icon when a notification arrives and Otty isn't focused
appearance.font_family_tab_computed_desc: Read-only — what actually renders right now
appearance.font_family_fallback_disabled: Disabled — this style is off in Text

key_bindings.no_results_keys: Nothing is bound to this shortcut
key_bindings.sequence_help: Bind a key to send literal bytes to the focused terminal. Action prefixes:
key_bindings.recipe_empty: No recipes have a shortcut assigned yet.
key_bindings.recipe_edit_hint: Edit shortcuts and create new recipes in the Recipes tab.
key_bindings.global_hotkey_help_windows: System-wide shortcuts that work even while another app is in front. Show Otty brings Otty forward, opening a window if none is open. Show / Hide Otty does the same, but minimizes Otty when it is already in front. Include Ctrl, Alt or Shift.
key_bindings.global_hotkey_help: System-wide shortcuts that work even while another app is in front. Show Otty brings Otty forward, opening a window if none is open. Show / Hide Otty does the same, but hides Otty when it is already in front. Use a modifier (⌘/⌥/⌃/⇧).

agents.codex_restore_warning: Codex is installed, but its Otty integration isn't — Codex sessions won't be restored. Click to install or ignore.
agents.group_agents_desc: Connect Otty to your coding agents for real-time badges, notifications, and session recovery.
agents.hook_desc: Adds Otty's hooks to {path} for real-time state updates
agents.launch_command_desc: Optional executable, wrapper and global flags. Otty appends the agent's own resume or fork arguments.
agents.needs_hooks_hint: Install hooks for at least one agent first
agents.badge_processing_desc: Show a tab badge while an agent is running a task
agents.badge_task_complete_desc: Show a tab badge when an agent finishes a task
agents.badge_awaiting_input_desc: Show a tab badge when an agent is waiting for you
agents.notify_task_complete_desc: Send a system notification when an agent finishes a task
agents.notify_awaiting_input_desc: Send a system notification when an agent is waiting for you
agents.prevent_sleep_desc: Keep Windows awake while an agent is running a task
agents.resume_session_desc: Reattach the agent's session when a window is restored
agents.plan_quota_desc_claude: Run `claude -p "/usage"` in the background every few minutes to read your session and weekly limits. Uses the login the CLI already has — no sign-in, no stored credential.
agents.plan_quota_desc_codex: Ask `codex app-server` in the background every few minutes for your account's rate limits. It answers from the server, so the reading stays right while this machine is idle and counts what you spent elsewhere. Uses the login the CLI already has — no sign-in, no stored credential.
agents.plan_quota_desc_omp: Run `omp usage --json` in the background every few minutes to read the spend limits of every account you have signed in. Uses the logins the CLI already has — no sign-in, no stored credential.
agents.group_skills_desc: Teach your coding agent to drive Otty. Copy a skill, paste it into the agent, and it writes the file itself.
agents.skill_wait_desc: Block until a command, agent session, or pane / tab / window finishes
agents.skill_tell_desc: Send a message to an agent session, window, tab, or the active pane
agents.skill_open_desc: Open a file or URL in a split, a new tab, or a new window
agents.skill_otty_desc: Drive Otty itself — lay out panes, run work or another agent in them, wait, collect
agents.skill_sheet_desc: Copy the installer prompt, then paste it into your coding agent.
agents.skill_name_hint: Installs as ~/.claude/skills/{name}/SKILL.md and is invoked as /{name}. Rename it if that collides with a skill you already have.
agents.skill_name_hint_empty: Enter a name — letters, digits, dash or underscore.
agents.skill_send_keys: Allow agents to type into panes
agents.skill_send_keys_desc: Required by this skill (ipc-allow-send-keys). Without it every send is refused. SSH and sudo panes still refuse input.
agents.skill_copied: Copied — paste it into your coding agent to install /{name}
agents.skill_copy_failed: Could not write to the clipboard — nothing was copied

advanced.reset_all_warnings_hint: Also clears every “always allow” security choice, including agent integration prompts.

view.osc_title_desc: Let programs rename the tab and window with OSC 0/1/2. Turn off to pin every tab to what these rules resolve.
view.projects_desc: One row per match. Open a row to set its alias, icon and title together.

alias.label: Project Alias
alias.desc: A short name for a project, also available as ${alias} in title templates.

icon.label: Icon
icon.desc: Shown on the tab. Pick from the set or type any emoji, then give it a colour.

title.label: Title
title.desc: Tab title template. Click a variable to insert it at the cursor.
title.fallback: Chain names with | to fall back when one is empty: ${title|folder|'Shell'} takes the first that has a value.

var.alias: The project alias resolved for this tab
var.cwd: Working directory, with the home folder shortened to ~
var.folder: Last path component of the working directory
var.user: SSH user, or the local user
var.host: SSH host — empty for local sessions
var.agent: Coding agent bound to the pane, if any
var.title: Title the program itself set
var.index: Position of the tab in its window
var.file: File name, for file / folder / URL panes

view.projects_dialog_desc: Set this project's alias, icon and title.
view.badge_exit_status_desc: Show accent dot on tab when a command finishes
view.badge_activity_desc: Show error alert on tab when a command fails
view.badge_awaiting_input_desc: Detect [y/n], password and ENTER prompts and show the awaiting-input badge

details.group_desc: Which tabs the details panel offers, in order. Drag a row to move it.
details.toggle: Show this tab in the details panel

builtin_desc.info: Folder, command, shell and host for the focused pane
builtin_desc.outline: Jump between the commands run in this pane
builtin_desc.git: Branch, status and changed files of the pane's repository
builtin_desc.files: Browse the working folder, with drag and drop

details.dialog_desc: Run a program in a terminal inside the panel, or load a page in a web view.
details.name: Name
details.mobile_hint: Load the page the way a phone browser would ask for it, so a site serves the layout written for a column this narrow. Off asks for the desktop page; either way the page is laid out at the panel's own width. Changing this reloads the view.
details.folder_hint: Where the program runs. Click a variable to follow the focused pane. Leave empty to give this view its own folder under ~/.config/otty/views.
details.shared_hint: Views that resolve to the same command and folder share one running program across every window — so a ${cwd} view gets one per directory. A view may not open windows, tabs, panes or GUI apps.
details.command_hint: Runs the way a prompt would, so pipes, `&&` and `;` work. Click a variable to insert it; quote it yourself if the value may contain spaces.

var.cwd: Working directory of the focused pane
var.folder: Last path component of that directory
var.file: File the focused pane has open, if any
var.pid: Process id of the focused pane
var.command: Command running in the focused pane
var.host: SSH host — empty for local panes
var.user: SSH user, or the local user
var.agent: Coding agent bound to the pane, if any

view.placement_desc: Whether the tab icon and status badge share one slot
view.placement_hint: Combined keeps one indicator: your icon, replaced by a status badge while something is happening. Separate puts the icon left and badges right, and hides the shell name — a split tab still shows its pane count.

webpane.persist_desc: Keep cookies and site data on disk, so sign-ins survive a restart
webpane.persist_hint: Off browses in memory: panes still share one session, but it is gone once the last web pane closes. Applies to panes opened after the change.
webpane.clear_desc: Cookies, site data, cache and history of every web pane
webpane.clear_hint: Turning “Stay Signed In” off does not remove what was already saved.
webpane.clear_dialog_body: Signs out of every site open in a web pane and empties their cache and history. This cannot be undone.
webpane.clear_failed: Could not clear everything — close your web panes and try again.

quick_access.group_desc: Pinned things to reopen — a folder, a recipe, an SSH host, a profile. The first five appear in the new-tab menu, the tray menu and the taskbar jump list, in this order.

updater.ready_to_install: Ready to install — quit Otty to apply the update.
updater.feed_unavailable: Update feed not available yet. Try again later.
updater.install_ready_message: Otty %@ is ready. Quit and reopen to finish the update.
updater.up_to_date_message: Latest version is %@, your version is %@.

dialog.caffeinate_message: Prevent system sleep while tasks run in this tab.
dialog.create_branch_message: Enter the name for the new branch:

file_search.preview_empty: Pick a result to preview it here.

error.no_ripgrep: ripgrep is missing from this build.

palette.no_forkable_agent: No fork-capable agent session in the focused pane

priv.keep_awake_any_task: Keep Awake While Any Task Runs

toast.dividers_unavailable_grouping: Dividers are not available while grouping is active
toast.pip_unsupported: This pane does not support Picture in Picture yet

tmux_scroll_hint.toast: tmux isn't reading the mouse — run `tmux set -g mouse on` to scroll its history

run_link.toast: Typed at the prompt — press Enter to run it, or ⌫ to clear.
run_link.multiline_unsupported: This link carries a multi-line script, and this shell did not advertise bracketed paste — the newlines would run the first lines before you could read them. Nothing was typed.
run_link.confirm_title: Type this command into a new tab?
run_link.confirm_body: A link in this terminal wants Otty to open a new tab and type the command below at the prompt. Nothing runs until you press Enter.
run_link.sync_confirm_body: A link asked Otty to start syncing this tool's config files to your other machines. You can change what is synced any time in Settings → Data.
run_link.sync_unavailable_body: Data Sync is a feature preview. Turn on Feature Preview in Settings → Advanced, then open this link again.
run_link.sync_not_installed: Otty doesn't see {app} on this device. It syncs a tool's config files once that tool is installed here.

remote_command.no_connection: No live connection to {host} — reconnect and try again
remote_command.folder_unsupported: Otty cannot open a remote folder yet — use the Files tab
remote_command.bad_path: Otty could not resolve that path: {path}
remote_command.record_failed: Otty could not update its folder list for {path}
remote_command.offer_body: A {size} script at ~/.local/share/otty/bin/otty, so `otty view` and `otty jump` typed there reach this Otty.
remote_command.installed: Installed `otty` on {host} — it takes effect the next time you ssh to {host}

remote_file.too_large: {path} is {size} — larger than Otty opens on its own
remote_file.no_cache: Otty has nowhere to keep a copy of remote files.
remote_file.needs_key: This host needs a key or ssh-agent sign-in for Otty to transfer files.

pill.title: Remote Access
pill.accessibility: Remote Access is watching this pane
pill.details_hint: Show who is on this pane
pill.stop_revokes_link: Stopping a share-link viewer revokes its link, so it can't reconnect.
pill.always_note: Take over is set to Always, so your own devices can come back at any time. Set it to Ask to be able to stop them here.

menu.needs_pin: A PIN is required but none is set yet, so every join will be refused. Set one in Settings › Remote.

join.title: Join a Remote Session
join.pick_host: Choose a device from My Devices to take over.
join.paste_title: Paste a Device Code or Share Link
join.paste_help: Paste the Otty device sign-in link or session share link from the other device.
join.pin_help: The six digits the host shows in Settings › Remote. Leave blank if the host does not ask for one.
join.pin_wrong: Wrong PIN. {n} tries left before it is retired.
join.pin_retired: Three wrong tries retired that host's PIN. Someone has to set a new one on the host before anybody can join.
join.host_disabled: That host is not accepting sessions right now.
join.not_paired: This host no longer recognises this device. Sign in again or request a new share link.
join.no_panes: That host is not sharing any panes.
join.link_revoked: Too many wrong PINs, so that link has been revoked. Ask for a new one.
join.pick_device: Choose one of your devices to take over.
join.pin_help_link: This link is protected by a PIN. Enter the six digits that came with it.
join.pin_wrong_link: Wrong PIN. {n} tries left before the link is revoked.
join.unreachable: The free plan connects two of your devices. Upgrade to Otty Anywhere Pro to reach this one.
join.waiting_body: Someone at {host} has to click Allow. If nobody does within a minute, the takeover is declined.

client.relay_pro: No direct connection was possible, and relaying needs Otty Anywhere Pro.
client.no_secret: The key for this connection is missing. Sign in again or request a new share link.
client.approval_timeout: Nobody on {host} answered in time, so the takeover was declined.

share.off_body: Open Settings › Remote and turn on Remote Access, then allow sharing before creating a link.
share.pin_first_body: A PIN is required to join this device, but none is set yet — the link would let nobody in. Choose six digits; anyone opening the link types them.
share.pin_invalid_body: A PIN is exactly six digits.
share.pro_title: Shared links need Otty Anywhere Pro
share.pro_body: Connecting your first two account devices is free. Sharing a session by link is part of Pro. Sign in from Settings › Remote to upgrade.
share.title: Share this session
share.with_pin: Send the link and the PIN separately — the link alone does not let anyone in. Anyone with both can open it from any device, as often as they like, until it expires or you revoke it.
share.without_pin: This link is the whole key: anyone who has it can join until it expires. Turn on a PIN in Settings › Remote to need both, and to let a link last longer.
share.no_pin_hint: No PIN is set for this device
share.intro: Anyone who opens this link can watch this pane — and type into it, if you allow typing.
share.link_is_key: Without a PIN this link is the whole key: anyone who has it can join until it expires.
share.no_random: This Mac could not generate a PIN.
share.pin_separately: Send the link and the PIN separately — the link alone does not let anyone in. Three wrong PINs revoke the link.
share.struck_out_body: Three wrong PINs were tried on the link to {pane}. Make a new link if you still want to share it.

unpair.relay_pending: Removed here. The relay has not confirmed yet — Otty will finish that the next time this device is online.

helper.offer_body: The helper reports host stats and browses files over the connection you already have. It installs two files under ~/.local/share/otty and opens no network ports.
helper.remove_nothing: The host reports nothing to remove.

approval.body_type: It will see this pane and can type into it. Nothing is shown until you allow it.
approval.body_view: It will see this pane, read-only. Nothing is shown until you allow it.
approval.notify_body: Allow or deny it on this Mac within a minute.
approval.title: ‘{device}’ wants to take over {pane}

account_lost.removed_title: This device was removed from your Otty account
account_lost.removed_body: Data Sync has stopped. Your files and settings on this device are untouched.
account_lost.wiped_body: Data Sync has stopped and this device's sync data was cleared, as requested. Your files and settings on this device are untouched.
account_lost.signed_out_title: You were signed out of Otty Anywhere
account_lost.signed_out_body: Data Sync has stopped. Sign in again in Settings › Account to carry on.
account_lost.wipe_failed_body: Data Sync has stopped, but its data on this device could not be cleared yet. Otty will try again.
account_lost.removed_body_plain: This device can no longer reach your other devices. Sign in again in Settings › Account to rejoin.
account_lost.signed_out_body_plain: This device can no longer reach your other devices. Sign in again in Settings › Account to carry on.

roster.joined_body: It can now reach your devices. If this wasn't you, remove it in Settings › Account.

trust.body: It will be able to reach your devices.
trust.failed_code: Warning: someone entered a wrong code for this device.
trust.failed_codes: Warning: someone entered {n} wrong codes for this device.
trust.only_if_you: Only allow this if you are signing in on that device right now.
trust.recovering: It is recovering the account and gets in on {date} unless you deny it.
trust.send_failed_body: Answer the request again in Settings › Account.
trust.send_failed_title: Your answer didn't reach Otty Anywhere
trust.title: Allow ‘{name}’ ({platform}) to join your Otty account?
trust.title_noplatform: Allow ‘{name}’ to join your Otty account?
trust.web_body: It is signed in to your account on the web and wants to remove a device or change how new devices get in.
trust.web_only_if_you: Only allow this if you are doing that in a browser right now.
trust.web_title: Allow ‘{name}’ to change your Otty account?
trust.web_title_unnamed: Allow a web browser to change your Otty account?

remote.via_helper: via the Otty helper, every 2 s
remote.via_helper_version: via the Otty helper {version}, every 2 s
remote.save_body: Otty writes a Host block to its own ssh_config so this machine has a name you can type. Your ~/.ssh/config is not rewritten.
remote.helper_unsupported: This platform has no helper build
remote.helper_failed: Could not reach the helper on {host}
remote.remote_commands_unsupported: This host cannot run it (no POSIX shell)
remote.remote_commands_needs_key: Otty on Windows installs it over a second ssh connection, so the host has to take a key or ssh-agent sign-in.
remote.remote_commands_host_key: Its SSH host key is not in known_hosts, so Otty will not connect to it on its own. Open an ssh session to it yourself and accept the key.
remote.save_to_configure: Save this connection to configure it
remote.scope_otty_body: Saved to Otty's host list. Plain `ssh <alias>` in other terminals won't know it.
remote.scope_both_body: Also adds one Include line at the top of ~/.ssh/config so ssh, scp and everything else can use the alias.
